sections.name: Settings (part 1)
sections.title: List of settings
sections.what: Declares every configurable value with its default: server address, database, AI provider and model names, search key, Redis, cache and embedding model.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app run with sensible defaults and override them.
sections.watch_out: Renaming a setting breaks any .env file that uses the old name.

sections.name: Settings: get_data_dir
sections.title: Folder and model-name helpers
sections.what: Creates the data and cache folders when asked, and returns the model name for a given agent type from the chosen provider.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps model selection in one place so switching providers is one setting.
sections.watch_out: An unknown agent type silently uses the research model, which can hide typos.

summary: Central place that reads settings from environment variables and the .env file and provides the model name for each agent type.
purpose: Holds the app's configurable values, such as database address, AI provider and model names, in one place.
why: Likely reason: keeps keys and choices out of the code.
how: The Settings class declares each setting with a default. Values from the .env file or environment override the defaults. Two helpers create folders on request. The model helper picks a model name based on the provider and agent type. One shared settings object is created when the file loads.
inputs: The .env file, environment variables and the defaults in the code.
outputs: The settings object used across the backend, model name text and created folders.
risks: Defaults point to local services such as Ollama, Redis and a SQLite file that may not exist. The research cache default is a Linux path and will fail or create odd folders elsewhere. Unknown agent types silently fall back to the research model. Missing keys produce no error at startup.
debug: If the wrong model runs, check model_provider and the environment. If a key is ignored, check the .env file is in the backend folder and the name matches. For folder errors, check permissions on the cache path.
